research_question: Can separating lifecycle-operation decisions from memory-content generation reduce complete-system cost while preserving question-answering quality and evidence-traceable memory state in natural-language interaction?

arms.B: same strong LLM operation-target decision plus common writer
arms.C: frozen Jev operation-target decision plus the exact B writer

primary_quality_comparison.metric: official-protocol per-question LongMemEval QA correctness over all 500 questions
primary_quality_comparison.decision_rule: noninferior only if the lower endpoint of the two-sided 95% paired-bootstrap confidence interval is greater than -0.03

cost_condition.metric: counterfactual standalone complete-system variable cost, excluding evaluator
cost_condition.decision_rule: the quality-cost claim succeeds only if C is noninferior to B and C costs at least 10% less than B
cost_condition.shared_artifacts: physically cached common work is charged in full to every arm for standalone attribution

secondary_analyses: A vs B isolates decision-generation separation
C vs A reports the complete architectural replacement contrast
paired McNemar tests with effect sizes and confidence intervals
evidence-traceable state contamination and omission on a prediction-blinded, preselected audit sample
complete-system p50, mean, and p90 stage and end-to-end latency

required_cost_reporting.local_compute_rule: report model, hardware, calls, tokens if available, and device time; do not label unmonetized local compute as free

interpretation_guardrails: Failure to reject a difference is not evidence of equivalence.
A numerical final-state advantage is not a stability advantage without paired uncertainty.
Controller-only cost ratios are not complete-system savings.
A filtered or construct-consensus subset is sensitivity analysis, not a replacement benchmark.
No universal Jev-over-frontier-LLM claim is permitted from this experiment.
